media.technicalReason: For distances between 101m and 400m (350m requested), OM4 50/125 µm Multimode Fiber with 10GBASE-SR transceivers provides low-loss optical interconnectivity. OM4 features an effective modal bandwidth (EMB) of 4700 MHz·km at 850nm, supporting 10Gbps transmissions up to 400m.
assumptions: High-quality 850nm Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSEL) used in SFP+ optics.
Connector insertion losses strictly kept below 0.75 dB combined total.
Internal campus/building riser or duct installation.
limitations: Modal dispersion limits bandwidth at longer distances; cannot be extended beyond 400m for 10Gbps (or beyond 100m for 40G/100G without MPO parallel optics).
Requires delicate bend radius management and LC fiber optic patch panels.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 100m physical channel limit by 250m; violates IEEE 802.3an attenuation limits.
Functionally capable but single-mode transceivers (10GBASE-LR) are significantly more expensive than 10GBASE-SR optics for links under 400m.

routing.protocol: Single-Area OSPF (Open Shortest Path First v2 - Area 0)
routing.architecture: Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) - Single Backbone Area
rfcReferences: RFC 3101: The OSPF Not-So-Stubby Area (NSSA) Option
routing.technicalExplanation: For a single autonomous system with 6 subnets (fewer than 50 threshold), Single-Area OSPF (Backbone Area 0) is optimal. OSPF uses Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to calculate loop-free paths with rapid sub-second convergence. Because the Link-State Database (LSDB) remains compact under 50 subnets, CPU and memory overhead during SPF recalculations is negligible, obviating the configuration complexity of multi-area partitioning.
routing.convergenceNotes: Sub-second failure detection via OSPF Hello/Dead intervals (10s/40s standard, or fast hellos/BFD for sub-50ms convergence) with immediate Link State Advertisement (LSA) flooding on link state changes.
routing.summarizationPlan: Route summarization is not required inside a single area because all OSPF routers maintain identical LSDBs; summarization occurs at Area Border Routers (ABRs) or Autonomous System Boundary Routers (ASBRs).

areaDesign.description: Core and distribution switches participate in single backbone link-state graph.

alternativesRejected.reason: Cisco-proprietary lineage (RFC 7868 informational); lacks open multi-vendor interoperability and standardization guarantees.
Distance-vector protocol with 15-hop limit, slow timer-based convergence (up to 180 seconds), and high bandwidth consumption due to periodic broadcast/multicast updates (RFC 2453).
Heavy path-vector protocol with extensive memory requirements and slower convergence; excessive operational complexity for an internal single-site LAN.

topology.description: High-speed switched Core backbone interconnecting independent Distribution blocks per building, aggregating dual-homed Access switches.
topology.technicalJustification: For 1600 endpoints distributed across 3 buildings, a 3-Tier Campus model isolates faults, permits non-blocking line-rate backbone routing at the core, encapsulates broadcast domains at the distribution layer, and provides deterministic RSTP convergence.

coreSwitch.title: Core/Distribution Switch Configuration
coreSwitch.content:
! =====================================================================
! NetArchitect Generated Configuration
! Device: Core / Distribution Layer Switch 01
! Hostname: CAMPUS-LAN-ENTERPRISE-CORE-SW01
! Platform Assumption: Cisco Catalyst 9500 / 9300 (IOS-XE 17.9+)
! =====================================================================
version 17.9
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
service password-encryption
!
hostname CAMPUS-LAN-ENTERPRISE-CORE-SW01
!
boot-start-marker
boot-end-marker
!
! Management & Security Baselines
enable secret 9 $9$PlaceholderCoreSecret$NetArchitect
!
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
aaa authorization exec default local
username netadmin privilege 15 secret 9 $9$AdminSecret$2026Net
!
ip routing
ip domain name netarchitect.internal
ip ssh version 2
ip ssh time-out 60
ip ssh authentication-retries 3
!
! Spanning Tree Protocol (IEEE 802.1w Rapid-PVST+)
! Root Bridge Primary Configuration
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree extend system-id
spanning-tree vlan 1-4094 priority 4096
!
! VLAN Database Definitions
vlan 999
 name QUARANTINE_NATIVE
!
vlan 10
 name Student_&_Staff_Wi-Fi
!
vlan 20
 name Academic_Labs_&_Workstations
!
vlan 30
 name Faculty_&_Administration
!
vlan 40
 name Campus_Data_Center_&_Servers
!
vlan 50
 name VoIP_Telephony_&_Surveillance
!
vlan 99
 name Network_Infrastructure_Management
!
! 802.1Q Core Downlink Trunks to Access Layer
! Platform note: Modern Cisco Catalyst 9000 switches use IEEE 802.1Q exclusively.
! Obsolete 'switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q' command is rejected on Cat 9000 and therefore omitted.
interface range TenGigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 4
 description 10G OM4/OS2 SFP+ 802.1Q Downlink Trunks to Access Switches
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50,99
 switchport nonegotiate
 spanning-tree guard root
 no shutdown
!
! Port-Channel Inter-Switch Link (LACP - Core Redundancy)
interface Port-channel1
 description LACP Inter-Chassis Core Cross-Connect
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50,99
 no shutdown
!
interface range TenGigabitEthernet1/0/47 - 48
 description LACP Core Member Bundle
 channel-group 1 mode active
!
! Switched Virtual Interfaces (SVIs) - Default Gateways
interface Vlan10
 description SVI Gateway for Student & Staff Wi-Fi [VLAN 10]
 ip address 10.10.0.1 255.255.252.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan20
 description SVI Gateway for Academic Labs & Workstations [VLAN 20]
 ip address 10.10.4.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan30
 description SVI Gateway for Faculty & Administration [VLAN 30]
 ip address 10.10.6.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan40
 description SVI Gateway for Campus Data Center & Servers [VLAN 40]
 ip address 10.10.8.1 255.255.255.128
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan50
 description SVI Gateway for VoIP Telephony & Surveillance [VLAN 50]
 ip address 10.10.8.129 255.255.255.128
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan99
 description SVI Gateway for Network Infrastructure Management [VLAN 99]
 ip address 10.10.9.1 255.255.255.192
 no shutdown
!
! Dynamic Routing Protocol: OSPF Process 1
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.255.255.1
 log-adjacency-changes
 passive-interface default
 no passive-interface Vlan10
 no passive-interface Vlan20
 no passive-interface Vlan30
 no passive-interface Vlan40
 no passive-interface Vlan50
 no passive-interface Vlan99
 network 10.10.0.0 0.0.3.255 area 0
 network 10.10.4.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.6.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.8.0 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.10.8.128 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.10.9.0 0.0.0.63 area 0
!
! Line Security
line con 0
 exec-timeout 5 0
 logging synchronous
 login authentication default
line vty 0 4
 exec-timeout 10 0
 transport input ssh
 logging synchronous
 login authentication default
!
end
write memory

! =====================================================================
! NetArchitect Generated Configuration
! Device: Border / WAN Edge Router 01
! Hostname: CAMPUS-LAN-ENTERPRISE-EDGE-RTR01
! Platform Assumption: Cisco ISR 4451 / ASR 1001-X (IOS-XE 17.9+)
! =====================================================================
version 17.9
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
service password-encryption
!
hostname CAMPUS-LAN-ENTERPRISE-EDGE-RTR01
!
enable secret 9 $9$PlaceholderRtrSecret$NetArchitect
!
ip routing
ip cef
!
! Core LAN Facing Interface (Downlink to Core Switches)
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 description Downlink to LAN Core Switch 01
 ip address 10.255.0.1 255.255.255.252
 ip ospf 1 area 0
 no shutdown
!
! WAN / Carrier Facing Interface
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 description WAN Uplink to Carrier Provider / EVPL
 ip address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.252
 ip access-group WAN_INBOUND_FILTER in
 no shutdown
!

!
! Internal Dynamic Routing: OSPF Process 1
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.255.255.254
 log-adjacency-changes
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 network 10.10.0.0 0.0.3.255 area 0
 network 10.10.4.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.6.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.10.8.0 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.10.8.128 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.10.9.0 0.0.0.63 area 0
!
! Static Default Route to Carrier Gateway
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 198.51.100.1
!
! WAN Edge Security Filter
ip access-list extended WAN_INBOUND_FILTER
 remark Block Inbound RFC 1918 Private Addresses (Anti-Spoofing)
 deny ip 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 any
 deny ip 172.16.0.0 0.15.255.255 any
 deny ip 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255 any
 remark Permit Established State Sessions
 permit tcp any any established
 remark Permit Essential ICMP Diagnostics
 permit icmp any any echo-reply
 permit icmp any any unreachable
 permit icmp any any time-exceeded
 remark Permit IPsec VPN Tunnels
 permit esp any host 198.51.100.2
 permit udp any host 198.51.100.2 eq isakmp
 permit udp any host 198.51.100.2 eq non500-isakmp
 remark Deny All Other Inbound Traffic
 deny ip any any log
!
end
write memory

explanations.decision: Selected OM4 Laser-Optimized Multimode Fiber (MMF 50/125 µm)
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Rule 5.B: 101m <= Distance <= 400m -> OM4 Laser-Optimized Multimode Fiber (850nm VCSEL)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Distance 350m exceeds 100m copper limit by 250m; within 400m OM4 modal bandwidth threshold (4700 MHz·km at 850nm).
explanations.technicalExplanation: For distances between 101m and 400m (350m requested), OM4 50/125 µm Multimode Fiber with 10GBASE-SR transceivers provides low-loss optical interconnectivity. OM4 features an effective modal bandwidth (EMB) of 4700 MHz·km at 850nm, supporting 10Gbps transmissions up to 400m.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 100m physical channel limit by 250m; violates IEEE 802.3an attenuation limits.
Functionally capable but single-mode transceivers (10GBASE-LR) are significantly more expensive than 10GBASE-SR optics for links under 400m.

assumptions: High-quality 850nm Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSEL) used in SFP+ optics.
Connector insertion losses strictly kept below 0.75 dB combined total.
Internal campus/building riser or duct installation.

explanations.decision: Selected Optical Interface: 10GBASE-SR SFP+ (850nm Short Reach)
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Transceiver Reach Selection vs Optical Power Budgeting
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Total Power Budget = Min Launch Power (-7.3 dBm) - Max Rx Sensitivity (-9.9 dBm) = 2.6 dB. Channel Insertion Loss = Fiber Loss (0.35 km x 3 dB/km = 1.05 dB) + Connector Loss (0.75 dB) + Splice Loss (0.1 dB) = 1.9 dB. Calculated Net Optical Margin = 2.6 dB - 1.9 dB = 0.7 dB (Pass / Sufficient Margin).
explanations.technicalExplanation: The transceiver module was selected based on transmitter launch power, photodetector sensitivity, dispersion penalty over distance, and operating wavelength (850 nm (VCSEL Laser)). Selecting higher-powered optics (such as ZR on a short link) could saturate the optical receiver diode, while insufficient optics would fail bit-error-rate thresholds.

alternativesRejected.reason: Lacks modularity; SFP+ allows field replacement and sparing flexibility.

assumptions: Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM/SFF-8472) enabled on all optical transceivers.
Receiver dynamic range is not exceeded; attenuators installed if power exceeds max receiver input.

explanations.decision: Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) Allocations for 6 Departments
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Descending-Order Binary Radix Tree Subnet Allocation (RFC 4632 / CIDR)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Root Network: 10.10.0.0/20 contains 4096 total IP addresses. Allocated: 2368 addresses across 6 subnets. Address Space Utilization: 57.8%. Remaining Free Space: 1728 addresses.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Subnet requests were sorted strictly in descending order of host requirements prior to allocation. This deterministic ordering prevents memory fragmentation and guarantees that every allocated subnet starts on a naturally aligned binary address boundary (where starting address mod 2^(32 - prefix) == 0). Network and broadcast addresses are mathematically preserved, preventing subnet overlap or silent address overflow.
explanations.standardsReference: RFC 4632 (Classless Inter-domain Routing) & RFC 1918 (Private Address Allocation)

alternativesRejected.technology: Classful Subnetting (FLSM / Fixed Length Subnet Masking)
alternativesRejected.reason: Forces uniform mask (e.g. /25 for all departments), causing severe address exhaustion and waste for small departments.
Causes address fragmentation where larger blocks cannot find continuous aligned binary boundaries.

assumptions: Standard LAN segments reserve 2 addresses (Network ID and Directed Broadcast).
The first usable IPv4 address in each subnet is designated as the Default Gateway (SVI).

explanations.decision: Selected Single-Area OSPF (Open Shortest Path First v2 - Area 0)

inputParameters.architecture: Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) - Single Backbone Area

explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Dijkstra SPF Shortest-Path First Link-State Routing with Area Hierarchies
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: SPF Time Complexity: O(E + V log V) where V = 9 nodes, E = 14 links. Database scale remains well within sub-second Dijkstra recomputation limits (<15ms compute overhead).
explanations.technicalExplanation: For a single autonomous system with 6 subnets (fewer than 50 threshold), Single-Area OSPF (Backbone Area 0) is optimal. OSPF uses Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to calculate loop-free paths with rapid sub-second convergence. Because the Link-State Database (LSDB) remains compact under 50 subnets, CPU and memory overhead during SPF recalculations is negligible, obviating the configuration complexity of multi-area partitioning.

alternativesRejected.reason: Cisco-proprietary lineage (RFC 7868 informational); lacks open multi-vendor interoperability and standardization guarantees.
Distance-vector protocol with 15-hop limit, slow timer-based convergence (up to 180 seconds), and high bandwidth consumption due to periodic broadcast/multicast updates (RFC 2453).
Heavy path-vector protocol with extensive memory requirements and slower convergence; excessive operational complexity for an internal single-site LAN.

assumptions: All OSPF Area 0 routers maintain contiguous backbone adjacencies.
Point-to-point OSPF network type configured on all routed inter-switch links to bypass DR/BDR election latency.

explanations.decision: IEEE 802.1w Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (Rapid-PVST+) & 802.1Q Tagged Trunks
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol Proposal-Agreement Handshake (RFC 802.1w)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Convergence time reduced from 30-50 seconds (Legacy 802.1D Spanning Tree) to < 1.0 second (802.1w Rapid-PVST+) via direct edge-port PortFast transitions and point-to-point proposal-agreement handshakes.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Rapid-PVST+ is configured with explicit bridge priority tuning. Core Switch 01 is configured with Priority 4096 (Root Primary), and Core Switch 02 with Priority 8192 (Root Secondary). Access switches use default 32768. BPDU Guard is enabled on all access edge ports to instantly error-disable ports if rogue switches are attached, preventing accidental root bridge takeover. Native VLAN is changed to an unused quarantine VLAN 999 to mitigate VLAN hopping attacks.

alternativesRejected.reason: Slow 30 to 50 second convergence timers (Listening and Learning states) disrupt mission-critical traffic and VoIP streams.
Leaves trunk open to VLAN hopping and unauthorized broadcast domain leakage; native VLAN 1 presents documented security vulnerabilities.

assumptions: Uplink interfaces configured as Point-to-Point full-duplex to enable RSTP rapid transitions.
BPDU Guard enabled globally on all PortFast access ports.

explanations.decision: Strict Priority Low-Latency Queuing (LLQ) with Sub-5ms Target Analysis
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Fiber Optical Time of Flight (ToF) & Differentiated Services (DiffServ / RFC 2474)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Light propagation in silica fiber core (refractive index n ≈ 1.468): v = c / n = 299,792 km/s / 1.4682 ≈ 204,190 km/s (4.898 µs/km). One-way fiber flight delay for 0.35 km = 1.71 µs. Round-Trip Time (RTT) pure fiber propagation = 0.003 ms. Remaining latency budget for switch serialization, queuing, and carrier transport: 4.997 ms.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Do NOT guarantee sub-5ms latency merely because QoS is enabled! Latency is governed by fundamental physics and carrier transport. While the pure optical propagation delay across 0.35 km is 0.003 ms, the total end-to-end latency experienced depends on: (1) Carrier route curvature/trench routing factor (typically 1.3x - 1.5x physical distance), (2) DWDM optical transponder regeneration, (3) Buffer queuing delays, and (4) Store-and-forward switch serialization delay. QoS Low-Latency Queuing (LLQ / Expedited Forwarding DSCP 46) eliminates queuing jitter for voice and high-priority financial packets, but cannot reduce the physical optical propagation constant.
explanations.standardsReference: RFC 2474 (DiffServ Architecture), RFC 3246 (Expedited Forwarding PHB), ITU-T G.8261

alternativesRejected.reason: Large bulk file transfers induce bufferbloat, increasing latency spikes well above 20-50ms.

assumptions: Carrier EVPL path does not exceed 1.4x straight-line fiber trench distance.
Core interfaces run at 10Gbps line-rate with hardware cut-through or fast store-and-forward switching.
warnings: Sub-5ms latency SLA requires strict carrier SLA commitments and verification via RFC 2544 / ITU-T Y.1564 BERT testing; QoS configuration alone cannot overcome transmission distance.

decisions.decision: Selected OM4 Laser-Optimized Multimode Fiber (MMF 50/125 µm)
decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Rule 5.B: 101m <= Distance <= 400m -> OM4 Laser-Optimized Multimode Fiber (850nm VCSEL)
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Distance 350m exceeds 100m copper limit by 250m; within 400m OM4 modal bandwidth threshold (4700 MHz·km at 850nm).
decisions.technicalExplanation: For distances between 101m and 400m (350m requested), OM4 50/125 µm Multimode Fiber with 10GBASE-SR transceivers provides low-loss optical interconnectivity. OM4 features an effective modal bandwidth (EMB) of 4700 MHz·km at 850nm, supporting 10Gbps transmissions up to 400m.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 100m physical channel limit by 250m; violates IEEE 802.3an attenuation limits.
Functionally capable but single-mode transceivers (10GBASE-LR) are significantly more expensive than 10GBASE-SR optics for links under 400m.

assumptions: High-quality 850nm Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSEL) used in SFP+ optics.
Connector insertion losses strictly kept below 0.75 dB combined total.
Internal campus/building riser or duct installation.

decisions.decision: Selected Optical Interface: 10GBASE-SR SFP+ (850nm Short Reach)
decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Transceiver Reach Selection vs Optical Power Budgeting
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Total Power Budget = Min Launch Power (-7.3 dBm) - Max Rx Sensitivity (-9.9 dBm) = 2.6 dB. Channel Insertion Loss = Fiber Loss (0.35 km x 3 dB/km = 1.05 dB) + Connector Loss (0.75 dB) + Splice Loss (0.1 dB) = 1.9 dB. Calculated Net Optical Margin = 2.6 dB - 1.9 dB = 0.7 dB (Pass / Sufficient Margin).
decisions.technicalExplanation: The transceiver module was selected based on transmitter launch power, photodetector sensitivity, dispersion penalty over distance, and operating wavelength (850 nm (VCSEL Laser)). Selecting higher-powered optics (such as ZR on a short link) could saturate the optical receiver diode, while insufficient optics would fail bit-error-rate thresholds.

alternativesRejected.reason: Lacks modularity; SFP+ allows field replacement and sparing flexibility.

assumptions: Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM/SFF-8472) enabled on all optical transceivers.
Receiver dynamic range is not exceeded; attenuators installed if power exceeds max receiver input.

decisions.decision: Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) Allocations for 6 Departments
decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Descending-Order Binary Radix Tree Subnet Allocation (RFC 4632 / CIDR)
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Root Network: 10.10.0.0/20 contains 4096 total IP addresses. Allocated: 2368 addresses across 6 subnets. Address Space Utilization: 57.8%. Remaining Free Space: 1728 addresses.
decisions.technicalExplanation: Subnet requests were sorted strictly in descending order of host requirements prior to allocation. This deterministic ordering prevents memory fragmentation and guarantees that every allocated subnet starts on a naturally aligned binary address boundary (where starting address mod 2^(32 - prefix) == 0). Network and broadcast addresses are mathematically preserved, preventing subnet overlap or silent address overflow.
decisions.standardsReference: RFC 4632 (Classless Inter-domain Routing) & RFC 1918 (Private Address Allocation)

alternativesRejected.technology: Classful Subnetting (FLSM / Fixed Length Subnet Masking)
alternativesRejected.reason: Forces uniform mask (e.g. /25 for all departments), causing severe address exhaustion and waste for small departments.
Causes address fragmentation where larger blocks cannot find continuous aligned binary boundaries.

assumptions: Standard LAN segments reserve 2 addresses (Network ID and Directed Broadcast).
The first usable IPv4 address in each subnet is designated as the Default Gateway (SVI).

decisions.decision: Selected Single-Area OSPF (Open Shortest Path First v2 - Area 0)

inputParameters.architecture: Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) - Single Backbone Area

decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Dijkstra SPF Shortest-Path First Link-State Routing with Area Hierarchies
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: SPF Time Complexity: O(E + V log V) where V = 9 nodes, E = 14 links. Database scale remains well within sub-second Dijkstra recomputation limits (<15ms compute overhead).
decisions.technicalExplanation: For a single autonomous system with 6 subnets (fewer than 50 threshold), Single-Area OSPF (Backbone Area 0) is optimal. OSPF uses Dijkstra's Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to calculate loop-free paths with rapid sub-second convergence. Because the Link-State Database (LSDB) remains compact under 50 subnets, CPU and memory overhead during SPF recalculations is negligible, obviating the configuration complexity of multi-area partitioning.

alternativesRejected.reason: Cisco-proprietary lineage (RFC 7868 informational); lacks open multi-vendor interoperability and standardization guarantees.
Distance-vector protocol with 15-hop limit, slow timer-based convergence (up to 180 seconds), and high bandwidth consumption due to periodic broadcast/multicast updates (RFC 2453).
Heavy path-vector protocol with extensive memory requirements and slower convergence; excessive operational complexity for an internal single-site LAN.

assumptions: All OSPF Area 0 routers maintain contiguous backbone adjacencies.
Point-to-point OSPF network type configured on all routed inter-switch links to bypass DR/BDR election latency.

decisions.decision: IEEE 802.1w Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (Rapid-PVST+) & 802.1Q Tagged Trunks
decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol Proposal-Agreement Handshake (RFC 802.1w)
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Convergence time reduced from 30-50 seconds (Legacy 802.1D Spanning Tree) to < 1.0 second (802.1w Rapid-PVST+) via direct edge-port PortFast transitions and point-to-point proposal-agreement handshakes.
decisions.technicalExplanation: Rapid-PVST+ is configured with explicit bridge priority tuning. Core Switch 01 is configured with Priority 4096 (Root Primary), and Core Switch 02 with Priority 8192 (Root Secondary). Access switches use default 32768. BPDU Guard is enabled on all access edge ports to instantly error-disable ports if rogue switches are attached, preventing accidental root bridge takeover. Native VLAN is changed to an unused quarantine VLAN 999 to mitigate VLAN hopping attacks.

alternativesRejected.reason: Slow 30 to 50 second convergence timers (Listening and Learning states) disrupt mission-critical traffic and VoIP streams.
Leaves trunk open to VLAN hopping and unauthorized broadcast domain leakage; native VLAN 1 presents documented security vulnerabilities.

assumptions: Uplink interfaces configured as Point-to-Point full-duplex to enable RSTP rapid transitions.
BPDU Guard enabled globally on all PortFast access ports.
